subject: Recap + Action Plan: Embeddings + Rerank POC, SDK + Function-calling Requirements
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@novatech.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + Action Plan: Embeddings + Rerank POC, SDK + Function-calling Requirements

Hi Elena — great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through Novatech's current search rerank workflow and the two pilot use-cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Pain points you confirmed:
- Current reranker is slow at scale (p95 latency ~720ms) and expensive because embedding store fetches are not batched.
- Existing ranked results drift after weekly model updates; you need deterministic rerank behavior for compliance.
- Mobile app needs streaming partial results for perceived latency.

Goals discussed:
1) Build a 6-week POC to replace the current reranker for product search in the US region.
2) Meet p95 < 200ms on production-like traffic for rerank path.
3) Maintain deterministic outputs for audit (stable seed + pinned model version).

Product fit notes (how Redwood maps to those goals):
- Embeddings + fast nearest-neighbor: recommend Redwood embeddings with prefix cache; can reduce fetches via batched multi-ids.
- Rerank as a streaming function: we can serve an initial lightweight scorer (fast) and stream detailed rerank scores back as they compute.
- Function-calling / structured outputs: for integration with your ingestion pipeline we propose a small contract where Redwood returns a JSON payload with {ranked_ids, scores, provenance: {model_version, seed}}.
- SDK work: minimal changes to Novatech client — one new streaming handler and a small schema change to accept the provenance block.

Immediate action items I propose:
- Redwood: deliver an annotated SDK diff + sample streaming handler by Friday (Nov 13). (Owner: Connor)
- Novatech: share anonymized sample logs for the rerank path (500 sessions) and your seed/pinning constraints. (Owner: Elena)
- Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60-min session next week with your infra + our runtime team to validate latency and KV-cache behavior. (Owner: Rishi to coordinate)

Attachments: I attached a short MVP spec and a connector matrix to show integration options.

If that matches your read, we can lock the POC kickoff for week of Nov 23 and draft a mutual action plan (timeline + success metrics).

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the SDK diff and calendar invites.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
---
Attachment stubs: novatech_mvp_spec.pdf (6 pages, diagram + success criteria), connector-matrix.xlsx (sheet: auth, latency expectations)

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 18:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap + Action Plan: Embeddings + Rerank POC, SDK + Function-calling Requirements

Connor — thanks for the clear summary and for the quick turnaround on next steps. That all looks right to me. A couple of clarifications:

1) The 500 sessions for logs are a sample of anonymized request/response pairs from production (no user PII). I can export and share by Thursday EOD.
2) For determinism we have a constraint that model_version must be explicitly stored in the event log — that’s fine.
3) For the mobile streaming case, we only need the partial ranked list within 150ms on warm cache; final scores can arrive inbound within 1s.

We’re open to kickoff the POC week of Nov 23. I’ll also loop in our infra lead (Marco) for the deep-dive.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Search & Relevance | Novatech AI
elena@novatech.ai

Perfect — appreciate the quick confirmation, Elena.

Rishi and I will:
- Prepare an SDK diff that demonstrates: (a) streaming handler signature, (b) structured JSON payload with provenance, and (c) an example of batched embedding fetch.
- Share an initial latency projection with assumptions (cache hit rate, batch size) by Friday.
- Send calendar invites for two meetings:
   • Technical deep-dive (60 min) — proposed: Tue Nov 17, 10:00 - 11:00 PT (will include Marco + our runtime engineer)
   • POC kickoff planning (30 min) — proposed: Wed Nov 18, 11:00 - 11:30 PT

One quick question for Elena: can you confirm who on your side will own data transfer (S3 push vs temporary access role)? That will determine the connector approach in the matrix.

I’ll attach the SDK diff as a gist/drive link when ready and ping the invites.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Connor
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Prep for Novatech deep-dive + SDK notes (internal)

Quick internal note following Elena's reply — thread summary for our prep: 

Key technical constraints to validate in the deep-dive:
- Mobile partial return within 150ms on warm cache (we need to test p95 under 50k qps spike sim).
- Determinism: ensure model_version + seed are surfaced in structured payload and persisted in audit logs.
- Connector: clarify S3 push vs role-based access (ask Marco). If role-based, we should pre-build a short-lived IAM role template.

SDK diff outline (Rishi + Connor):
- Add StreamingRerankHandler interface: on_partial(list), on_final(list, provenance)
- Add explicit provenance object in returned JSON: { model_version, seed, timestamp }
- Client backwards compatibility: default to non-streaming path if handler not provided

Action owners:
- Rishi: runtime latency projection + test plan (assumptions doc) by Fri 11/13.
- Aisha: draft commercial POC scope and pricing (1-month pilot, pricing bands) by Mon 11/16.
- Connor: SDK diff + calendar invites by Fri 11/13.

I’ll drop the test harness skeleton in the shared drive link and attach it to the HubSpot deal.

— Connor
